# Your money is stuck. You deserve answers.
**By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha**  
**10 November 2026**

Since Friday, 6 November, you have not been able to withdraw your money from Pinha.

Our payments partner, Northvale Payments, blocked all outgoing transfers at 09:00 that morning, without warning. Deposits and round-ups have stopped too.

Your money is not lost. It remains in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money. Northvale cannot use it for its own business. But we cannot move it until Northvale releases it.

That distinction matters. It also does not pay your rent.

I’m Inês. I’m a product designer at Pinha, and I write a lot of the words you see in the app. Today I’m writing something I wish none of us needed to read: what happened, what we got wrong, and what you can do while we work to get your money moving again.

## First: if you urgently need access to your money

If you need your savings for **rent, medical costs, or because you have lost your job**, please email:

**urgent@pinha.example**  
**Subject: URGENTE**

Tell us briefly what you need and when you need it. We are trying to obtain individual releases from Northvale for urgent cases.

**We cannot guarantee a release or a date.** I wish we could. But please contact us so we can raise your case.

Our three-person support team has received around 1,900 emails since Friday. Replies are currently taking about two days. That is a long time to wait when the question is about your own money. We are reading and answering, even if you have not heard back yet.

We have also cancelled the monthly Pinha fee for **November and December for everyone**. You should not be paying us while you cannot access your savings. This does not make up for what is happening.

## What happened

Pinha is a round-up savings app. Northvale Payments, an electronic money institution based in Vilnius, is the partner that holds customer funds.

On **4 November**, Northvale emailed us a notice of “commercial termination”, giving us 30 days’ notice. The explanation they provided was a “risk appetite review”. They did not give us a substantive reason beyond that.

Then, on **6 November at 09:00**, they blocked all outgoing transfers without warning, before that notice period had ended and contrary to what their notice said.

That is why you cannot withdraw. Deposits and round-ups have also stopped.

On **7 November**, we filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank.

Our CEO, Rui, is spending today in calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal. We are pursuing the release of your funds and the steps needed to move to a new partner. Those conversations matter, but conversations are not the same as getting your money back into your hands. We know that.

## Where your money is

Your money remains in a **safeguarded account**, separate from Northvale’s own funds. It is not money Northvale can use to run its business.

The problem is access: Northvale has blocked outgoing transfers, and we cannot move the funds until they release them.

We want to be precise here. Saying your money is safeguarded is not the same as saying everything is fine. Everything is not fine. Savings you cannot reach when you need them are not doing the job you trusted us to help them do.

We will keep explaining both parts: where the money is, and what is preventing you from accessing it. You deserve more than a reassuring sentence without the rest of the facts.

## We have signed a new partner. The move is not complete.

We have already signed with **Ostra Bank in Lisbon**.

To migrate, we need Northvale to send the balances file, and we need approval from Banco de Portugal. Signing a new partner does not let us bypass those steps or move the money ourselves.

Our current estimate for the migration is **10 to 15 working days**. **That is an estimate, not a promised withdrawal date.** It depends on steps we do not fully control, including Northvale providing the file and the required approval.

We do not have a confirmed date when you will be able to withdraw again. We will not turn an estimate into a deadline just because a deadline would make this post easier to write.

If the estimate changes, we will tell you.

## Northvale made this decision. We made a mistake too.

I am angry at Northvale. Giving notice and then blocking access before that notice period ends leaves people carrying the consequences of a decision they had no part in.

“Risk appetite review” is the explanation we received. It does not answer the question our users are asking: why can’t I take out my own money?

But blaming Northvale is not the whole account.

**We relied on one payments partner. We did not have a backup ready. That was our mistake.**

We were naive about what that dependence could mean. Now you are the ones waiting.

You chose Pinha. You did not choose our partner arrangements, and it was not your job to check whether we had another route ready if one failed. It was ours.

We are sorry. Not because we need an apology somewhere in this post, but because we gave you a reason to trust us and have not delivered what you had every right to expect.

You are entitled to be angry at Northvale. You are entitled to be angry at us too. I am not going to ask you to calm down.

## These are not just balances on a screen

One person wrote to us in capital letters. She had saved for three years for a car deposit, and the dealer had given her until Friday, 13 November.

I read her email on the metro and nearly cried.

I do not say that to ask for sympathy. My feelings do not help her meet that deadline. I say it because “withdrawals are suspended” sounds bloodless compared with what it actually means in someone’s life.

It means years of putting a little aside, then finding you cannot use it at the moment you planned to.

I designed the screen that says: **“Your money is always yours, take it out anytime.”**

I look at it now and feel sick. The money is still yours. Right now, the second half of that sentence is not true. I helped write a promise that our service is failing to keep.

## What happens next

We are working to get Northvale to release funds, obtain the balances file, and complete the migration to Ostra Bank with the required approval. We are also seeking individual releases for urgent cases.

We will publish updates on this blog **every Monday and Thursday until this is resolved**, starting with **Thursday, 12 November**.

We will say what has changed, what is still blocked, and whether our estimate still holds. If there is no progress, we will say that too. Silence should not leave you guessing.

For now:

- **If your need is urgent:** email **urgent@pinha.example**, with **URGENTE** in the subject, and briefly explain your situation and deadline.
- **If you are waiting for a support reply:** our current response time is around **two days**.
- **For progress updates:** check this blog on **Mondays and Thursdays**.
- **For fees:** November and December’s monthly fees have been cancelled for everyone.

You do not owe us patience or a kind email. We owe you answers, honest updates, and the work needed to restore access to your money.

— Inês
